evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/person-months.tsx:77-91 — `useBuildingUnits` runs `await fetch(`/api/v1/units?buildingId=${buildingId}&limit=500`, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })` inside a TanStack `useQuery` queryFn. This is a RAW browser `fetch`, not the shared axios instance.

The app injects the JWT ONLY via the axios request interceptor in frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:198-204 (`requestConfig.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`` from the token provider registered in contexts/AuthContext.tsx:327 `setTokenProvider(getAccessToken)`). A raw `fetch()` does not pass through axios, and the call sets no `Authorization` header and no `credentials: 'include'`. There is NO global fetch override, service worker, or cookie-based session in the app (grep for `globalThis.fetch =`/`window.fetch =`/`credentials: 'include'`/`serviceWorker` returns nothing outside tests). So this request to the authenticated management endpoint `/api/v1/units` goes out with no bearer token — it will 401 for a real logged-in session, and the building-units dropdown that feeds the person-months screen silently fails to populate.

Systemic, not a one-off: the same header-less raw-fetch-to-`/api/v1/*` pattern recurs across the news feature — features/news/pages/EditArticlePage.tsx:115 (PUT), CreateArticlePage.tsx:55 (POST), ArticleDetailPage.tsx:43-45,112,135 — all hitting authenticated endpoints with only a `Content-Type` header and no Authorization. (Those live in the ppt-web-ui segment; person-months.tsx in routes/ is the in-segment instance and the anchor for this finding.) App.tsx:71 `/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify` is the ONE legitimate raw fetch — it runs pre-auth before a token exists.

Secondary defects in the same block: (a) the response is hand-typed with an `as { data: Array<{ id: string; unitNumber: string }> }` cast that bypasses the generated `@ppt/api-client` types, so it will drift silently from the OpenAPI contract; (b) `limit=500` is hard-coded with no follow-up pagination, so a building with >500 units silently drops the overflow from the dropdown.

Fix: route this through the shared axios `api` instance (or the generated `@ppt/api-client` units call) so the JWT interceptor attaches the bearer token and the response is typed from the OpenAPI schema; drop the hand-written `as` cast; and either page through all units or document/raise the 500 cap. Self-contained TS change in routes/groups/person-months.tsx (+ optionally sweep the news pages); no backend/migration/mobile dependency — fully landable in the cloud runner.

Confidence medium: the axios-only token injection (lib/api.ts:198-204), the raw fetch, and the absence of any global fetch/cookie fallback are all confirmed by static read; 'medium' rather than 'high' because an actual 401 was not reproduced at runtime in this static-only pass (a dev proxy or an as-yet-unseen mitigation could in principle mask it).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/iot.tsx:180-184 — the sensor-delete confirmation is a HARDCODED English literal: `window.confirm(`Delete sensor "${sensor.name}"? This removes its readings and alerts and cannot be undone.`)` — not wrapped in `t(...)`. Slovak/Czech/German users (the product's primary locales, i18n sk/cs/de/en) see raw English on a destructive-action prompt.

This is a local inconsistency, not a codebase-wide convention: the SAME file's threshold-delete confirm at iot.tsx:545-549 correctly uses `t('iot.thresholdDeleteConfirm', { defaultValue: 'Delete this threshold? This cannot be undone.' })`, and routes/groups/faults.tsx:262-266 uses `t('faults.confirmDelete', { defaultValue: 'Delete this fault? This action cannot be undone.' })`. The sensor-delete path was simply missed.

Fix: wrap the sensor-delete message in `t('iot.sensorDeleteConfirm', { defaultValue: 'Delete sensor "{{name}}"? This removes its readings and alerts and cannot be undone.', name: sensor.name })` and add the key to the sk/cs/de/en resource bundles, mirroring the existing `iot.thresholdDeleteConfirm` entry. Trivially self-contained TS/i18n change; no backend/mobile dependency — fully landable.
Confidence high: the hardcoded literal and the two sibling `t()`-wrapped confirms in the same/adjacent files are directly visible; this is an unambiguous i18n gap on a user-facing string.
